paragraphs.source_en:
Asia
Who made that sense which, when the winds of spring
In rarest visitation, or the voice
Of one beloved heard in youth alone,
15 Fills the faint eyes with falling tears which dim
The radiant looks of unbewailing flowers,
And leaves this peopled earth a solitude
When it returns no more?

contains —] Nbk 8; contains? These lines are ungrammatical, as the second and third sub-clauses in the sentence both imply
a verb which is not present; the plural winds and singular voice cannot both govern Fills. There may
well be a hiatus in the text, although Nbk 8 does not differ significantly from 1820 or 1839, so there is
no basis for emendation in any witness. Presumably, sense governs both Fills and leaves; as for when in
line 12 would give a coherent reading. Asia appears to recall here her own words at the beginning of
